cases.explain: Дядя is the grammatical subject of the clause (он ... правил), so it must stand in the nominative case.
На брегах (on the banks) governs Невы in the genitive to express possession — the banks of the Neva.
The preposition к always requires the dative case, so театр becomes театру.

cases.sentence: Давно ли для вас я забывал ___ славы?
cases.explain: Жажду is the direct object of the transitive verb забывал (forgot), so it takes the accusative case.
The short passive participle окружена (surrounded) requires the instrumental of the agent/means, hence толпою.

cases.sentence: Не найдёт знакомых лиц на ___ скучной.
cases.explain: The preposition на indicating static location (where, not motion-to) requires the prepositional case, сцене.

reading.ru: Мой дядя самых честных правил, Когда ни в шутку за ним мог, Он уважать себя заставил, И лучше выдумать не мог.
reading.question: What is said about Onegin's uncle in the opening lines?
options: He has the strictest of principles
reading.correct: He has the strictest of principles
reading.explain: The poem opens by describing the uncle as a man of "the most honest rules," i.e., strict principles.

reading.ru: Так думал молодой Повеса, летя в пыли на почтовых.
reading.question: How is the young rake (Onegin) traveling as he has these thoughts?
options: Riding in a mail-coach, hurrying through the dust
reading.correct: Riding in a mail-coach, hurrying through the dust
reading.explain: The text says the young rake was "flying in the dust on post-horses," i.e., traveling by mail coach.

reading.ru: Родился на брегах Невы, где, может быть, родились вы.
reading.question: Where was Onegin born?
options: On the banks of the Neva
reading.correct: On the banks of the Neva
reading.explain: The text states he was born "на брегах Невы" — on the banks of the Neva, i.e., in St. Petersburg.

reading.ru: Давал три балла ежегодно и промотался на конец.
reading.question: What did Onegin's father do that eventually ruined him financially?
options: He gave three balls every year and eventually squandered his fortune
reading.correct: He gave three balls every year and eventually squandered his fortune
reading.explain: The text says the father "gave three balls annually and in the end squandered" his money.

reading.ru: Сперва мадам за ним ходила, потом мусье ее сменил.
reading.question: Who cared for young Onegin before the French tutor Monsieur arrived?
reading.correct: A madame (governess)
reading.explain: The text says "at first a madame looked after him, then a monsieur replaced her."

reading.ru: Когда же юности мятежной пришла Евгению пора, пора надежды, грусти нежной, мусье прогнали со двора.
reading.question: What happened to the French tutor Monsieur when Onegin reached the age of rebellious youth?
options: He was driven off/dismissed from the household
He was promoted to be Onegin's business partner
reading.correct: He was driven off/dismissed from the household
reading.explain: The text says "the monsieur was driven off the estate" once Onegin's turbulent youth arrived.

reading.ru: Вот мой Онегин на свободе, Острижен по последней моде, Как Дэнди лондонский одет, И, наконец, увидел свет.
reading.question: How is Onegin described once he gains his freedom (finishes his upbringing)?
options: Cropped in the latest fashion, dressed like a London dandy
reading.correct: Cropped in the latest fashion, dressed like a London dandy
reading.explain: The text describes him as "cropped in the latest fashion, dressed like a London dandy," entering society.

reading.ru: Так воспитанием, слава Богу, У нас не мудрено блеснуть».
reading.question: What does the narrator wryly say about this kind of upbringing?
options: Thanks to such an upbringing, it's no wonder one can shine in society
Only rigorous scholars succeed in society
Education is the most important virtue
Nobody in Russia receives an education
reading.correct: Thanks to such an upbringing, it's no wonder one can shine in society
reading.explain: The narrator ironically notes that with such an upbringing, "thank God, it's no wonder to shine" superficially.

reading.ru: Онегин был, по мнению многих судей решительных и строгих, ученый малый, но педант.
reading.question: How do the strict critics/judges regard Onegin?
options: A learned fellow, but a pedant
reading.correct: A learned fellow, but a pedant
reading.explain: The text says that in the opinion of many strict judges, he was "a learned fellow, but a pedant."

reading.ru: Бронил Гомера, Феокрита, зато читал Адама Смита и был глубокий эконом.
reading.question: Which author did Onegin actually read and admire, despite scorning classical poets like Homer?
reading.correct: Adam Smith
reading.explain: The text says he scorned Homer and Theocritus, "but read Adam Smith and was a deep economist."

reading.ru: Отец понять его не мог и земли отдавал в залог.
reading.question: What financial trouble does Onegin's father face?
reading.correct: He kept mortgaging/pawning his lands
reading.explain: The text says his father "could not understand him and kept giving his lands as collateral," i.e., mortgaging them.

reading.ru: Пока мест в утреннем уборе, надев широкий боливар, Онегин едет на бульвар.
reading.question: What hat does Onegin wear as he heads out to the boulevard?
reading.correct: A wide bolivar hat
reading.explain: The text specifies he put on "a wide bolivar" (a fashionable hat style) before heading to the boulevard.

reading.ru: Морозной пылью серебрится его бобровый воротник.
reading.question: What detail of Onegin's clothing is described as silvered with frosty dust?
reading.correct: His beaver fur collar
reading.explain: The text says "his beaver collar is silvered with frosty dust."

reading.ru: Театр, злой законодатель, Непостоянный обожатель Очаровательных актрис, Почетный гражданин кулис, Онегин полетел к театру, Где каждый критикой дыша Готов охлопать антроша, Обшикать Федру, Клеопатру, Маину вызвать для того, Чтоб только слышали его.
reading.question: How does the narrator describe the theater in this stanza?
options: A harsh lawgiver and a fickle admirer of charming actresses
A quiet, sacred place of worship
reading.correct: A harsh lawgiver and a fickle admirer of charming actresses
reading.explain: The narrator calls the theater "a harsh lawgiver, a fickle admirer of charming actresses."

reading.ru: Там в старые годы Сатиры смелый властелин Блистал фан-визин, друг свободы, И переменчивый княжнин.
reading.question: Which real-life Russian playwright, called "friend of freedom," is mentioned as having shone there in the old days?
reading.correct: Fonvizin
reading.explain: The text names "Fonvizin, friend of freedom" as having shone in the theater's earlier days.

reading.ru: Блистательно, полувоздушно, Смычку волшебному послушно, Толпою нимф окружена, Стоит истомина.
reading.question: Who is described as standing amid a crowd of nymphs, obedient to the magic bow (music)?
reading.correct: Istomina, the ballerina
reading.explain: The text says "surrounded by a crowd of nymphs, stands Istomina," the celebrated ballet dancer.

reading.ru: Двойной лорнет скосясь наводит на ложе незнакомых дам.
reading.question: What does Onegin do with his double lorgnette once inside the theater?
options: He aims it at the box of unfamiliar ladies
He gives it away to a friend
He drops it on the floor
He uses it to read a letter
reading.correct: He aims it at the box of unfamiliar ladies
reading.explain: The text says his "double lorgnette, squinting, aims at the box of unfamiliar ladies."

reading.ru: Балеты долго я терпел, но и дедло мне надоел.
reading.question: How does Onegin (the narrator's persona) feel about the ballets by this point?
options: Tired of them, bored even with the choreographer Didelot
Thrilled and wanting to see another
reading.correct: Tired of them, bored even with the choreographer Didelot
reading.explain: The text says "I endured ballets for a long time, but even Didelot has bored me," reflecting jaded weariness.

reading.ru: А уж Онегин вышел вон, Домой одеться едет он.
reading.question: What does Onegin do right after leaving the theater?
options: He goes home to change his clothes
He goes straight to a duel
He falls asleep in his carriage
reading.correct: He goes home to change his clothes
reading.explain: The text says Onegin "has left already, he's off home to dress" after the theater.

reading.ru: Увы, на разные забавы я много жизни погубил, но если б не страдали нравы, я балы б до сих пор любил.
reading.question: What does the narrator admit about his own past regarding amusements?
options: He squandered much of his life on various amusements
He devoted his life entirely to work
reading.correct: He squandered much of his life on various amusements
reading.explain: The narrator confesses, "Alas, on various amusements I squandered much of my life."

reading.ru: Люблю их ножки, только вряд найдете вы в России целой три пары стройных женских ног.
reading.question: What humorous claim does the narrator make about women's feet in Russia?
options: You'll hardly find three pairs of shapely women's feet in all of Russia
All Russian women have identical feet
Feet are not admired in Russian culture
Every woman in Russia has beautiful feet
reading.correct: You'll hardly find three pairs of shapely women's feet in all of Russia
reading.explain: The narrator jokes that "you will hardly find in all of Russia three pairs of shapely women's feet."

reading.ru: Что ж мой Онегин, полусонный, В постелью с бала едет он, А Петербург неугомонный, Уж барабаном пробужден.
reading.question: What is happening in St. Petersburg as sleepy Onegin heads home from the ball?
options: The restless city is being woken up by a drum
The city is completely silent and asleep
Church bells are ringing for a wedding
reading.correct: The restless city is being woken up by a drum
reading.explain: The text contrasts drowsy Onegin heading home with "the restless Petersburg, already awakened by the drum."

reading.ru: Нет, рано чувства в нем остыли.
reading.question: What does the narrator say happened to Onegin's feelings?
options: His feelings grew more passionate with age
He fell deeply in love for the first time
reading.correct: His feelings cooled early
reading.explain: The text states plainly, "No, his feelings cooled early," reflecting his growing ennui.

reading.ru: Он застрелиться, слава богу, Попробовать не захотел, Но к жизни вовсе охладел.
reading.question: What did Onegin, in his despondency, ultimately decide NOT to do?
reading.correct: Try to shoot himself
reading.explain: The text says "he did not try to shoot himself, thank God, but grew utterly cold to life."

reading.ru: И вы, красотки молодые, которых позднюю порой уносят дрожки удалые по Петербургской мостовой, и вас покинул мой Евгений.
reading.question: Whom does the narrator say Onegin abandoned, along with the pretty young women carried along the Petersburg pavement?
options: His former pursuit of society's pleasures and beauties
reading.correct: His former pursuit of society's pleasures and beauties
reading.explain: The text says Onegin, an apostate from stormy pleasures, also abandoned these pretty young women and society's diversions.

reading.ru: Отрядом книг уставил полку, читал, читал, а все без толку.
reading.question: What does Onegin do after stocking a shelf with books?
options: He reads and reads, but finds no use in it
He immediately writes his own novel
reading.correct: He reads and reads, but finds no use in it
reading.explain: The text says he "stocked a shelf with a detachment of books, read, read — but all to no avail."

reading.ru: Кто жил и мыслил, тот не может в душе не презирать людей.
reading.question: What does the narrator claim about anyone who has truly lived and thought deeply?
options: In his soul he cannot help but despise people
He will always love humanity unconditionally
reading.correct: In his soul he cannot help but despise people
reading.explain: The narrator states "whoever has lived and thought cannot help but despise people in his soul," a cynical reflection shared with Onegin.

highlight.question: What does the narrator's uncle do when he falls seriously ill?
highlight.explain: This line describes how he forces people to respect him through his honorable conduct during his illness.

highlight.question: What subjects does the uncle know about?
sentences: То есть умел судить о том,
highlight.explain: These lines describe him as a deep economist who understands how to judge matters of state.

highlight.question: What signal interrupts the pleasure of dining and drinking?
highlight.explain: These lines describe how the watch ring signals that the ballet has started, drawing people away from food.

highlight.question: What does someone bring along the Baltic waves to Russia?
sentences: За лес и сало возит нам,
Всё, что в Париже вкус голодный,
highlight.explain: These lines specify that forest and lard are brought across the sea as imports.

highlight.question: What does the narrator regret wasting in his younger years?
sentences: Но если б не страдали нравы,
Я балы б до сих пор любил.
highlight.explain: These lines express remorse about wasting much of his life on various entertainments.

highlight.question: How does the passage describe the monotonous nature of daily life?
sentences: И завтра то же, что вчера.
Но был ли счастлив мой Евгений,
highlight.explain: These lines convey that each day repeats the same pattern, with tomorrow being like yesterday.
